access-list.allowed-groups-help.defaultMessage: One per line. A directory user must be in at least one of these groups. Leave empty to accept anyone the provider authenticates. Usernames listed on the Authorizations tab are unaffected.

access-list.help-rules-last.defaultMessage: When at least 1 rule exists, this deny all rule will be added last

access-list.help.rules-order.defaultMessage: Note that the allow and deny directives will be applied in the order they are defined.

access-list.providers-intro.defaultMessage: Accept sign-ins from a directory as well as the usernames listed here. Visitors are still prompted for a username and password; those credentials are checked against the directory instead of the list.

access-list.providers-none.defaultMessage: No LDAP provider is set up yet. Add one under Users, Authentication Providers, and it will appear here. SAML and OAuth cannot be used: they sign people in by redirecting a browser, which is not possible for a proxied request.

auth-provider.admin-group-help.defaultMessage: Anyone in this group is given the admin role on every sign in, and loses it when they leave the group. Leave blank to manage roles here instead.

auth-provider.auto-create-user.defaultMessage: Create users on first sign in

auth-provider.auto-create-user-help.defaultMessage: When off, only people already linked to this provider can sign in. New accounts are never created.

auth-provider.delete-confirm.defaultMessage: Remove {name}? Nobody will be able to sign in through it afterwards.

auth-provider.delete-convert-help.defaultMessage: They keep their hosts, permissions and ownership, but hold no password yet. Set one for them from the Users screen so they can sign in again.

auth-provider.delete-no-users.defaultMessage: No accounts came from this provider, so nothing else is affected.

auth-provider.delete-users-help.defaultMessage: {removable, plural, =0 {None would actually be removed: they can all still sign in another way.} one {One account would be removed.} other {# accounts would be removed.}} Anyone who can still sign in another way is kept, and so is the last remaining administrator.

auth-provider.delete-users-intro.defaultMessage: {count, plural, one {One account came from this provider} other {# accounts came from this provider}}. What should happen to them?

auth-provider.delete-users-warning.defaultMessage: Deleting an account also removes what it owns. This cannot be undone.

auth-provider.empty-summary.defaultMessage: Add an LDAP directory, a SAML identity provider or an OAuth/OpenID Connect application to get started.

auth-provider.env-managed-help.defaultMessage: This provider is configured with environment variables and can only be changed by editing them.

auth-provider.intro.defaultMessage: Let people sign in with your existing directory or identity provider.

auth-provider.ldap.bind-dn-help.defaultMessage: A read-only service account used to look users up. Leave blank to search anonymously.

auth-provider.ldap.group-attribute-help.defaultMessage: Read from the user entry, if your directory provides it.

auth-provider.ldap.group-filter-help.defaultMessage: Used when the user entry has no group attribute. '{{dn}}' and '{{username}}' are substituted before searching.

auth-provider.ldap.login-attributes-help.defaultMessage: Comma separated attributes accepted at the login prompt, for example uid, mail, sAMAccountName. Ignored when a user filter is set.

auth-provider.ldap.page-size-help.defaultMessage: Directories cap how many entries one search returns, 1000 in Active Directory by default. Paging walks past that limit.

auth-provider.ldap.user-filter-help.defaultMessage: '{{username}}' is replaced with whatever was typed into the login form.

auth-provider.ldap.verify-tls-help.defaultMessage: Only turn this off for a directory using a self-signed certificate you trust.

auth-provider.link-by-email.defaultMessage: Adopt existing accounts by email address

auth-provider.link-by-email-help.defaultMessage: The first time someone signs in, attach them to an account here that already has the same email address. Only turn this on if you trust this provider to have proved the address belongs to them.

auth-provider.link-by-email-help-oauth.defaultMessage: The first time someone signs in, attach them to an account here that already has the same email address. The provider must also report the address as verified, otherwise anyone able to set their own could claim somebody else's account.

auth-provider.local-enabled.defaultMessage: Allow email and password sign in

auth-provider.local-enabled-help.defaultMessage: Turn this off to require an authentication provider. Make sure you can sign in with one first.

auth-provider.local-required-help.defaultMessage: Add and enable a provider before you can turn this off.

auth-provider.oauth.issuer-url-help.defaultMessage: Endpoints are discovered from here. Leave blank to configure them by hand below.

auth-provider.oauth.redirect-uri-help.defaultMessage: Add this to the allowed redirect URIs of your OAuth application.

auth-provider.oauth.use-basic-auth.defaultMessage: Send credentials in the Authorization header

auth-provider.oauth.use-basic-auth-help.defaultMessage: Some providers require client_secret_basic instead of sending the secret in the request body.

auth-provider.saml.identifier-attribute-.defaultMessage: Attribute holding a lasting id for each person, such as an employee number. Leave blank to use the NameID, or the email address when your IdP issues a transient NameID.

auth-provider.saml.issuer-help.defaultMessage: How this instance identifies itself to the identity provider.

auth-provider.saml.metadata-help.defaultMessage: Give this URL to your identity provider to configure the connection.

auth-provider.secret-stored.defaultMessage: A value is stored. Leave blank to keep it.

auth-provider.sync-disable-missing.defaultMessage: Disable accounts that leave the directory

auth-provider.sync-disable-missing-help.defaultMessage: The last remaining administrator is never disabled this way, and nothing is disabled if a run returns no entries at all.

auth-provider.sync-enabled.defaultMessage: Sync this directory on a schedule

auth-provider.sync-enabled-help.defaultMessage: Sync creates a local account for everyone it finds, whether or not they have ever signed in.

auth-provider.sync-filter-help.defaultMessage: Restricts which directory entries are considered.

auth-provider.sync-group-help.defaultMessage: Only sync members of this group. Leave blank to sync everyone the filter matches.

auth-provider.sync-interval-help.defaultMessage: Five minutes is the shortest interval allowed.

auth-provider.sync-intro.defaultMessage: Walks the directory on a schedule so accounts exist before anyone signs in, and so group changes are picked up without waiting for a login.

auth-provider.test-connection-help.defaultMessage: Checks the settings above without saving them, so you can confirm them before filling in the rest.
